skills.name: parametrize_conics_as_projective_space
skills.description: Identify the set of plane conics with the projective space P^5 by using the coefficients of a homogeneous quadratic form in three variables, modulo scaling.
skills.preconditions: Working over a field, consider homogeneous degree‑2 polynomials in variables x,y,z; two such polynomials represent the same conic iff they differ by a nonzero scalar.
skills.postconditions: A bijection between smooth conics and the open subset of P^5 where the discriminant is nonzero; the whole space of (possibly singular) conics is identified with P^5.
skills.example: Lines in P^2 are parametrized by P^2*: a linear form a x + b y + c z up to scaling gives a point (a:b:c) in P^2.

skills.name: express_tangency_as_incidence_condition
skills.description: Formulate the tangency of two conics C and D as the existence of a point p where both vanish and their gradients are linearly dependent.
skills.preconditions: Two conics given by quadratic forms f and g, and a point p ∈ P^2 with homogeneous coordinates.
skills.postconditions: A closed subvariety of P^5 × P^5 × P^2 defined by the equations f(p)=g(p)=0 and rank of the Jacobian matrix [∇f(p); ∇g(p)] ≤ 1.
skills.example: Two circles in the affine plane are tangent iff there is a point where their defining equations vanish and the normals (gradients) are parallel.

skills.name: project_incidence_to_conic_space_to_get_divisor
skills.description: Eliminate the point variable from the incidence variety of tangency to obtain a hypersurface in the space of conics representing the tangency condition.
skills.preconditions: Incidence subvariety defined as in the previous skill, with the projection map to the factor parametrizing the moving conic being proper and generically finite.
skills.postconditions: A divisor in P^5 given by a single homogeneous polynomial (the discriminant of the resultant) whose degree can be computed.
skills.example: Projecting the incidence of a line meeting a fixed smooth conic onto the dual projective plane yields the dual conic curve, a degree‑2 hypersurface.

skills.name: compute_degree_of_tangency_divisor_via_resultant
skills.description: Determine the degree of the hypersurface of conics tangent to a fixed conic by forming the resultant of the two quadratic forms and its Jacobian, which yields a homogeneous polynomial of known degree.
skills.preconditions: A fixed smooth conic C₀, the universal family of conics represented by coefficients (a₀:…:a₅), and knowledge of the resultant construction for two quadrics in three variables.
skills.postconditions: Explicit degree (equal to 2) of the tangency divisor in P^5.
skills.example: The discriminant of a binary quadratic form ax²+ bxy+ cy² is b²−4ac, a homogeneous polynomial of degree 2 in (a,b,c).

skills.name: apply_bezout_to_intersect_multiple_divisors
skills.description: Intersect k hypersurfaces of known degrees in projective space P^n and compute the number of isolated intersection points (with multiplicity) as the product of the degrees, assuming a transverse generic intersection.
skills.preconditions: Hypersurfaces H₁,…,H_k in P^n with degrees d₁,…,d_k, where k = n, and the hypersurfaces are in general position so that the intersection is zero‑dimensional and transverse.
skills.postconditions: The total number of intersection points counted with multiplicity equals d₁·d₂·…·d_k.
skills.example: Two distinct lines (degree 1) in P^2 intersect in exactly 1 point.

skills.name: use_generic_smoothness_to_get_finite_etale_projection
skills.description: Invoke the generic smoothness theorem to conclude that the projection from an incidence variety to the parameter space is smooth (hence étale) over a dense open subset, giving a finite étale morphism.
skills.preconditions: A morphism f : X → Y of finite type between varieties over a field, X smooth, and the generic fiber of f is zero‑dimensional.
skills.postconditions: Existence of a dense open U ⊂ Y such that f|_{f^{-1}(U)} : f^{-1}(U) → U is finite étale.
skills.example: The map (x, y) ↦ x from the graph of the polynomial y² = x³ + x over ℂ is étale away from the points where the derivative 2y = 0.

skills.name: relate_geometric_degree_to_average_fiber_size_over_finite_fields
skills.description: State that for a finite étale morphism of degree d defined over ℤ, the average number of ℱ_p‑rational points in its fibers over ℱ_p tends to d as p → ∞, by combining étaleness with the Lang–Weil estimate.
skills.preconditions: A finite étale morphism f : X → Y of degree d, both X and Y defined over ℤ, and p a prime of good reduction (i.e., f remains étale modulo p).
skills.example: The map ℙ¹ → ℙ¹ given by t ↦ t² is finite étale away from t=0,∞; the average number of square roots of a random element of ℱ_p is 2 as p grows.

skills.name: apply_lang_weil_estimate_for_point_counts
skills.description: Use the Lang–Weil theorem to approximate the number of ℱ_q‑points on a variety of dimension m and degree δ by q^m plus an error term of order q^{m-1/2}.
skills.preconditions: A geometrically irreducible variety V defined over a finite field ℱ_q, with known dimension m and degree δ.
skills.postconditions: An estimate |V(ℱ_q) - q^m| ≤ C·δ·q^{m-1/2} for some constant C depending only on m.
skills.example: A smooth plane curve of degree 3 (an elliptic curve) over ℱ_p has p + O(p^{1/2}) rational points.

skills.name: compute_enumerative_number_of_conics_tangent_to_five_conics
skills.description: Intersect the five tangency divisors (each of degree 2) in the parameter space P^5 and apply Bézout’s theorem to obtain the classical enumerative invariant – the number of smooth conics tangent to five generic conics.
skills.preconditions: Degree 2 of each tangency divisor (from Skill 4), generic choice of the five fixed conics so that the intersection is transverse and zero‑dimensional.
skills.postconditions: An integer count equal to 2⁵ = 32 multiplied by the appropriate multiplicity coming from the geometry, yielding the known number 3264 of conics tangent to five generic conics.
skills.example: The number of lines meeting four general lines in ℙ³ is 2, obtained by intersecting four hyperplane classes of degree 1 in the Grassmannian G(1,3).

skills.name: convert_enumerative_count_to_floor_of_scaled_limit
skills.description: Given the integer enumerative count N that equals the limit L, compute floor(100 L) by ordinary arithmetic.
skills.preconditions: The limit L is known exactly (often an integer) from previous enumerative calculation.
skills.example: If the enumerative count is N = 42, then floor(100·L) = floor(4200) = 4200.
